name: RC22 H1 (old): Loss Rebalancing (IS=0.005, VS=1.0)
result: 166a: 5/9 best, 4/9 final. S4 perfect (1.000), S8 median_bias PASS. But S2 still FAIL (spread tighter). IS reduction was the primary driver. Loss tuning reached its ceiling — architecture is the bottleneck.

name: RC22 H1 (v2): Factorized Decoder with Split Conditioning
theory: The decoder's attention trunk conflates conditional drift and stochastic factor structure. Post-attention noise injection via L@eps prevents rank compression. Split conditioning via FiLM.
result: 167a: 5/9 best (S3 regression), 5/9 final. eff_rank=2.55 (no improvement from baseline ~2). L_norm declined from 0.08 (ep10) to 0.01 (ep80) — factor path effectively died. CRPS satisfies itself with CLN rank-1 diversity. Architecture provides capacity but loss doesn't incentivize rank diversity. Key learning: architecture alone cannot solve rank compression without a rank-aware loss.

name: RC22 H2: K Reduction (K=8, B=32)
theory: SOTA uses K=2-4. Our K=16 has centering/spread ratio 1.07. K=8 gives 1.14.

name: RC22 H3: Encoder Contrastive Loss (conditional on H1 v2)
theory: Encoder condition 98% shared. InfoNCE pushes regimes apart. Only run if H1 v2's load_head produces constant L across windows (meaning 2% discriminative signal insufficient).
target: Encoder probe accuracy improvement. L variance across windows increases.
note: H1 v2 showed L varied across windows (L_var=0.000046, not zero) but L magnitude was too small to matter. The issue was not encoder discrimination but loss incentive for rank diversity.
